scope.summary: This standard specifies the material, shape, dimensions, workmanship, finish, and sampling requirements for detachable loop handles used with two-men cross cut saws conforming to IS 12127 : 1987, which are used for felling and cross-cutting trees of diameter more than 200 mm.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Certification. Manufacturers can apply to the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) to use the prestigious BIS 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) on the loop handles as a certified guarantee of material, dimensional, and workmanship quality. Compliance with IS 12627 is heavily specified by public sector forestry departments, logging state-cooperatives, and lumber procurement agencies across India.

requirements.detail: The wooden handle (Part 1) must be manufactured from high-quality, seasoned hardwood species resistant to splitting and impact: Acacia arabica (Babul), Acacia catechu (Khair), Anogeissus latifolia (Bakli), Adina cordifolia (Haldu), Azadirachta indica (Neem), Ougeinia dalbergioides (Sandan), Schleichera trijuga (Kusum), Shorea robusta (Sal), or Terminalia tomentosa (Laurel).
Wooden blanks must be completely free from centre heart (pith), decay (rot), checks, shakes, splits, borer holes, and warp to prevent structural failure or operator injury.

The Cap (Part 3), Washer (Part 4), and Nut (Part 2) must be made from mild steel conforming to IS 226 : 1975. The Loop Bolt (Part 5) must be made from high-strength spring steel conforming to IS 2507 : 1975.

To protect the hardwood handle from weather elements and moisture in wet forest environments, the standard recommends dipping the completed handles in raw linseed oil at about 90°C for exactly one hour immediately after manufacture.

The shapes and dimensions of loop handles must conform to the assembly and component details shown in Fig. 1A to 1C. Dimensional tolerances must satisfy the very coarse class specified in IS 2102 (Part 1) : 1980.
There must be absolutely no play in the loop bolt after tightening the nut. Forged components must be free from burrs, pits, sharp edges, cracks, and other physical defects, with well-formed threads.

Provides a major advantage over traditional permanent fixed clamps. In tree felling where felling wedges (IS 12191) are driven into the kerf to keep it open, the loop handles can be quickly detached from the saw, allowing the saw blade to be drawn out of the kerf from the end even under load.

Unless otherwise agreed, sampling to verify conformity must be conducted in accordance with Annex A. It mandates grouping handles of the same nominal size into a lot. The scale of sampling must follow Table 1 based on lot size, specifying the sample size and the maximum permissible number of defectives.

Any observed or calculated test or dimension value must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be identical to the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 12627 : 1989 is the national Indian Standard specification establishing technical requirements, material properties, and sampling plans for detachable wooden loop handles used with two-men cross cut saws. Developed under the Forestry and Plantation Machinery Sectional Committee (AFDC 64) and reaffirmed in 2024, this standard ensures the physical safety and structural reliability of loop handles during heavy logging operations. It mandates using high-quality seasoned hardwoods (like Sal, Babul, or Khair) free of structural defects, specifies mild steel for caps and nuts, and requires high-strength spring steel for the loop bolt. It also recommends dipping handles in raw linseed oil at 90°C for one hour to prevent weathering and establishes a systematic random sampling plan to verify lot quality.
